title: Beginner Pack 7
subtitle: Describing Things — Adjectives, Negative Forms & Clause Contrast
label: 3 patterns · 6 questions
rationale: Empowers learners to describe attributes and express nuanced contrasts using Level 1’s adjective 大きい (and companion vocabulary): (1) い-adjectives modify nouns directly (大きい山) or state properties as predicates (山は大きいです), (2) negative adjective ending 〜くないです allows stating that something is not big / not tall, and (3) conjunctive particle が joins two contrasting thoughts into a single compound sentence (Aですが、B = A, but B).
description: Learn い-adjectives modifying nouns and predicates, negative adjective ending 〜くないです, and clause contrast particle が.

patterns.readingNote: い-adjectives end in い and can sit right before a noun (大きい山) or before です at the end of a sentence (山は大きいです).
patterns.summary: In Pack 1, nouns were connected with の (駅の入り口). Adjectives like 大きい directly describe a noun without needing の (大きい山 = big mountain). When used as the main predicate, add です for politeness (あの山は大きいです = that mountain is big).

examples.japanese: ふじ山は大きい山です。
examples.reading: ふじさんは おおきい やまです。
examples.gloss: ふじ山 Mt. Fuji · 大きい big · 山 mountain · です is
examples.english: Mt. Fuji is a big mountain.

examples.reading: あの かわは おおきいです。
examples.gloss: あの川 that river · 大きいです is big/large

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form of the adjective to modify 山 (mountain):
questions.targetMeaning: Mt. Fuji is a big mountain.
questions.gloss: ふじ山 Mt. Fuji · 山 mountain · です is

choices.explanation: Not quite. 大きくに is not a valid modifier before a noun; い-adjectives modify directly with their dictionary form ending in い (大きい山).
Not quite. 大きさ is the noun “size,” which would require の to modify a noun (大きさの山); 大きい modifies directly.
That’s right! An い-adjective directly precedes the noun it modifies (大きい山 = big mountain).

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — Choose the correct adjective form to modify 木 (tree) in “There is a big tree near the river”:
followUp.japanese: 川の近くに（　）木があります。
followUp.targetMeaning: There is a big tree near the river.
followUp.reading: かわの ちかくに（　）きが あります。
followUp.gloss: 川の近く near the river · 木 tree · あります there is

choices.explanation: Not quite. 大きさ is the noun “size.” An adjective like 大きい modifies a noun directly.
That’s right! 大きい directly modifies 木 (大きい木 = big tree).
Not quite. 大きく is the adverbial/conjunctive stem, used before verbs (大きく書きます), not directly before a noun.

workedExample.japanese: 川の近くに大きい木があります。
workedExample.reading: かわの ちかくに おおきい きが あります。
workedExample.english: There is a big tree near the river.
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: Identify the noun to describe: 木 (“tree”). Step 2: Use the plain い-adjective directly: 大きい木 (“big tree”). Step 3: Complete with existence frame: 川の近くに…があります (“There is… near the river”).

questions.reading: あの かわは おおきいです。
questions.gloss: あの川 that river · は topic · 大きいです is big

choices.explanation: That’s right! あの川は sets “that river” as the topic, and 大きいです states the predicate “is big.”
Not quite. “Small” is 小さい (ちいさい); 大きい (おおきい) means “big / large.”

choices.text: There are big fish in the river.
choices.explanation: Not quite. This sentence describes the size of the river itself (川は大きいです), not items inside it.

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — What does this sentence mean?
followUp.reading: ふじさんは たかい やまです。
followUp.gloss: ふじ山 Mt. Fuji · 高い tall/high · 山 mountain · です is

choices.text: Mt. Fuji is a low mountain.
choices.explanation: Not quite. “Low” is 低い (ひくい); 高い (たかい) means “tall / high.”

choices.text: There is a mountain near Mt. Fuji.
choices.explanation: Not quite. This is an adjective identification sentence (AはBです), not an existence sentence.

choices.text: Mt. Fuji is a tall mountain.
choices.explanation: That’s right! ふじ山は is “Mt. Fuji,” and 高い山です is “is a tall mountain.”

workedExample.reading: ふじさんは たかい やまです。
workedExample.english: Mt. Fuji is a tall mountain.
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: Topic: ふじ山は (“Mt. Fuji”). Step 2: Modified noun: 高い山 (“tall mountain”). Step 3: Polite copula: です (“is”).

patterns.readingNote: Drop the final い of an い-adjective and add くないです to say “is not [adjective]”.
patterns.summary: To make an い-adjective negative, drop the final い and add くないです (大きい → 大きくないです = is not big; 高い → 高くないです = is not tall/expensive).

examples.japanese: この駅の入り口は大きくないです。
examples.reading: この えきの いりぐちは おおきくないです。
examples.gloss: この駅 this station · の of · 入り口 entrance · 大きくないです is not big
examples.english: The entrance of this station is not big.

examples.japanese: あの部屋は広くないです。
examples.reading: あの へやは ひろくないです。
examples.gloss: あの部屋 that room · 広くないです is not spacious/wide

questions.prompt: Choose the negative form that completes “The entrance of this station is NOT big”:
questions.targetMeaning: The entrance of this station is not big.
questions.reading: この えきの いりぐちは（　）。
questions.gloss: この駅 this station · 入り口 entrance

choices.explanation: Not quite. 大きいです is affirmative (“is big”), but we need the negative “is not big.”
That’s right! Drop the final い from 大きい and add くないです → 大きくないです (“is not big”).
Not quite. い-adjectives do not attach でした directly; the past form is 大きかったです, and neither is negative.

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — Choose the negative form that completes “That mountain is NOT tall”:

choices.explanation: That’s right! Drop い from 高い and add くないです → 高くないです (“is not tall”).
Not quite. じゃないです is used with nouns and な-adjectives, never with い-adjectives.
Not quite. でした does not attach to くない; the past negative is 高くなかったです.

workedExample.japanese: あの山は高くないです。
workedExample.reading: あの やまは たかくないです。
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: Start with plain adjective: 高い (“tall”). Step 2: Drop final い → 高 (taka). Step 3: Add negative ending 〜くないです → 高くないです (“is not tall”).

questions.japanese: この部屋は広くないです。
questions.reading: この へやは ひろくないです。
questions.gloss: この部屋 this room · 広くないです is not spacious

choices.explanation: Not quite. 広い (ひろい) means spacious, but 〜くないです is negative (“is not spacious”).

choices.text: This room has a wide door.
choices.explanation: Not quite. This describes the room itself, and the predicate is negative.
That’s right! この部屋は is “this room,” and 広くないです is the negative adjective predicate “is not spacious.”

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — What does this sentence mean?
followUp.japanese: あのビルは高くないです。
followUp.reading: あの ビルは たかくないです。
followUp.gloss: あのビル that building · 高くないです is not tall

choices.explanation: Not quite. 高いです is affirmative (“is tall”); 高くないです is negative (“is not tall”).
That’s right! あのビルは is “that building,” and 高くないです is “is not tall.”
Not quite. The sentence describes height with 高い (negative: 高くないです), not room count.

workedExample.japanese: あのビルは高くないです。
workedExample.reading: あの ビルは たかくないです。
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: Topic: あのビルは (“that building”). Step 2: Negative adjective predicate: 高くないです (“is not tall”).

patterns.readingNote: が connects two contrasting clauses, meaning “but” or “however.”
patterns.summary: You have seen が marking existence subjects (水があります). When placed between two complete clauses with a comma (〜ですが、…), が acts as a conjunction meaning “but” or “however” (小さいですが、明るいです = It is small, but bright).

examples.japanese: この部屋は小さいですが、明るいです。
examples.reading: この へやは ちいさいですが、あかるいです。
examples.gloss: この部屋 this room · 小さい small · ですが but · 明るい bright · です is
examples.english: This room is small, but it is bright.

examples.japanese: あのホテルは古いですが、きれいです。
examples.reading: あの ホテルは ふるいですが、きれいです。
examples.gloss: あのホテル that hotel · 古い old · ですが but · きれい clean/pretty · です is
examples.english: That hotel is old, but it is clean.

questions.japanese: この部屋は小さいですが、明るいです。
questions.targetMeaning: This room is small, but it is bright.
questions.reading: この へやは ちいさいですが、あかるいです。
questions.gloss: この部屋 this room · 小さい small · ですが but · 明るい bright · です is

choices.text: This room is small, but it is bright.
choices.explanation: That’s right! この部屋は is “this room,” 小さいですが is “is small, but,” and 明るいです is “is bright.”

choices.text: This room is small and dark.
choices.explanation: Not quite. While 小さい does mean “small,” 明るい (あかるい) means “bright,” not “dark,” and ですが expresses contrast (“but,” not “and”).

choices.text: This room is large and bright.
choices.explanation: Not quite. While 明るい does mean “bright,” 小さい (ちいさい) means “small,” not “large.”

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — What does this sentence mean?
followUp.japanese: あのホテルは古いですが、きれいです。
followUp.targetMeaning: That hotel is old, but it is clean.
followUp.reading: あの ホテルは ふるいですが、きれいです。
followUp.gloss: あのホテル that hotel · 古い old · ですが but · きれい clean/pretty · です is

choices.text: That hotel is old and dirty.
choices.explanation: Not quite. While 古い does mean “old,” きれい means “clean/pretty,” not “dirty,” and ですが expresses contrast (“but”).

choices.text: That hotel is new and clean.
choices.explanation: Not quite. While きれい does mean “clean,” 古い (ふるい) means “old,” not “new.”

choices.text: That hotel is old, but it is clean.
choices.explanation: That’s right! あのホテルは is “that hotel,” 古いですが is “is old, but,” and きれいです is “is clean.”

workedExample.japanese: あのホテルは古いですが、きれいです。
workedExample.reading: あの ホテルは ふるいですが、きれいです。
workedExample.english: That hotel is old, but it is clean.
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: First clause: あのホテルは古い (“That hotel is old”). Step 2: Add contrast conjunction: ですが、 (“is old, but”). Step 3: Second clause: きれいです (“it is clean”). Notice how が balances the drawback (old) with the positive feature (clean).

questions.japanese: 水はありますが、お茶はありません。
questions.targetMeaning: There is water, but there is no tea.
questions.reading: みずは ありますが、おちゃは ありません。
questions.gloss: 水 water · あります there is · ですが but · お茶 tea · ありません there is not

choices.text: There is both water and tea.
choices.explanation: Not quite. お茶はありません is negative (“there is no tea”), and ですが indicates contrast.

choices.text: There is water, but there is no tea.
choices.explanation: That’s right! 水はありますが means “there is water, but,” and お茶はありません means “there is no tea.”

choices.text: There is tea, but there is no water.
choices.explanation: Not quite. 水 (water) is affirmative with あります, while お茶 (tea) is negative with ありません.

followUp.prompt: Follow-up check — What does this sentence mean?
followUp.japanese: あの人は大人ですが、力はありません。
followUp.reading: あの ひとは おとなですが、ちからは ありません。
followUp.gloss: あの人 that person · 大人 adult · ですが but · 力 strength · ありません has not

choices.text: That person is an adult, but has no strength.
choices.explanation: That’s right! あの人は大人ですが is “that person is an adult, but,” and 力はありません is “has no strength.”

choices.text: That adult has great physical power.
choices.explanation: Not quite. ありません is negative (“does not have strength”), and ですが indicates contrast.
Not quite. This describes one person’s attributes using 大人 and 力, not multiple people waiting.

workedExample.japanese: あの人は大人ですが、力はありません。
workedExample.reading: あの ひとは おとなですが、ちからは ありません。
workedExample.english: That person is an adult, but has no strength.
workedExample.breakdown: Step 1: First clause: あの人は大人ですが (“That person is an adult, but”). Step 2: Contrasting second clause: 力はありません (“has no strength / power”).
